claim.purpose: Implement #5778 derived terminal truth and one idempotent finish command without a second closeout PR.

initial.title: Derive terminal truth and finish in one idempotent command
initial.goal: Replace the post-merge closeout transaction with derived terminal truth and one retry-safe typed finish command.
initial.required_outcome: An exact reviewed and green issue converges through merge and terminal confirmation without tracked post-merge mutation, a terminal receipt projection, or a second PR.
declared_scope: C-SDLC v2 terminal resolution and finish command
Focused lifecycle tests and operator contracts
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: One implementation issue needs one PR and successful finish creates no tracked post-merge diff or second PR
AC-2: Exact-head review, required checks, publication identity, and expected-SHA merge protection remain fail-closed
AC-3: Already-merged, interrupted-after-merge, and concurrent finish calls converge idempotently
AC-4: Merged, closed-unmerged, and approved no-PR outcomes derive from live GitHub and immutable Git truth
AC-5: Terminal remote state makes stale local claims non-blocking without deleting dirty work
AC-6: Legacy terminal records and receipts remain readable without rewrite
AC-7: Focused Gate 4-7 tests and strict Clippy pass
invariants: Never write tracked files on main
No AWS or external ledger service
No weaker review, checks, publication identity, or expected-head merge gate
No terminal projection or second closeout PR
Machine-readable JSON on stdout and human observability on stderr
non_goals: Standalone cleanup implementation owned by follow-on #5779
Runtime, provider, ADL language, or deployment changes
deliverables: Derived terminal resolver and typed result schemas
Exact-head and idempotent finish integration tests
Updated operator manifest and focused documentation
dependencies: GitHub API and Git graph remain canonical remote authorities
initial.failure_policy: Fail closed before merge on any stale digest, claim, review, head, check, publication, repository, PR, or no-PR authority mismatch; after a proven remote terminal event, retries must converge without requiring tracked state.
authority_boundary: Typed C-SDLC v2 Rust binaries only
GitHub mutation limited to expected-head merge and governed terminal observation
No raw lifecycle state or card edits
operator_constraints: Do not use AWS or Spot
Do not write tracked files on main
Keep implementation within the declared protected paths
Run a bounded subagent review before publication
initial.plan_summary: Characterize current closeout behavior; implement a pure derived terminal resolver; add csdlc-finish with exact-head merge and retry convergence; make terminal remote state non-blocking for claims while preserving legacy reads; validate focused Gate 4-7 behavior; obtain exact-head review and publish one ready PR.

steps.action: Add characterization fixtures and freeze the derived terminal input/output contract
Implement the pure terminal resolver and legacy compatibility classification
Implement csdlc-finish exact-head merge and interruption-safe idempotent convergence
Make proven terminal remote state non-blocking for claim collision and update operator contracts
Run focused validation, exact-head review, ready publication, and CI shepherding

validation_lanes.proof_role: Prove exact-head, terminal disposition, idempotency, interruption, concurrency, and legacy compatibility behavior
Preserve Gate 7 legacy lifecycle reads and claim safety while the new finish path is added
Prove warning-free C-SDLC v2 code across all targets

review_prompts: Does finish preserve exact reviewed-head, required-check, publication identity, and expected-SHA merge guarantees?
Can any interruption or concurrent call create conflicting terminal results or require a second PR?
Does terminal claim release avoid weakening active nonterminal collision safety?
Are legacy records readable without becoming competing current authority?
initial.review_scope: Issue #5778 C-SDLC v2 derived terminal resolver, finish binary, claim collision behavior, compatibility readers, focused tests, operator manifests, and docs.
risks: Treating a stale or unrelated GitHub observation as terminal could release a live claim
Review evidence committed after review could recreate exact-head recursion
Squash merge ancestry differs from head ancestry and must use GitHub merge identity truthfully
Compatibility logic could accidentally retain the old receipt as canonical
stop_conditions: Any need to weaken exact-head review or required checks
Any need for raw GitHub lifecycle mutation
Any collision with a live nonterminal claim
Any requirement for AWS, external persistence, or worktree deletion
Any design that still needs a second closeout PR
initial.task_boundary: Implement only the first serialized closeout-simplification slice: derived terminal truth and one idempotent finish command with compatibility reads; leave cleanup and deletion to #5779 and #5780.
